reviews.one_line_contribution: It edits the ALFWorld PDDL initial state so target objects sit off their class-canonical receptacle (deterministic per scene x class) and crosses that with a tight step budget and with three bank compositions, in order to show that an experience retriever beats the best static prompt only when the episode requires an instance binding that the bank supplies, and that a ~274-row compiled location table recovers the same gain with no per-episode uncached tokens.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three verified threats, none a full collision. (a) arXiv:2608.14036 'Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't' (2026-08-14, verified via s2cli paper) concludes that skills help by procedural anchoring rather than by injecting missing knowledge, and diagnoses retrieval bottlenecks and brittle assumptions - i.e. the proposal's framing claim that retrieval gains on template environments are procedure-bound is already stated there, though observed in a contrastive study rather than manipulated by editing the environment. The proposal does not cite it. (b) arXiv:2605.12493 LongMemEval-V2 (2026-05-12, cit 9, verified) is a benchmark for acquiring environment-specific experience in web environments whose two shipped methods are AgentRunbook-R (RAG over state observations/events/strategy notes) and AgentRunbook-C (a compiled trajectory store), compared on accuracy and latency - that is compiled-vs-retrieved at a cost axis, which is a substantial part of this proposal's P6 payload, again uncited. (c) The home-literature ancestor is arXiv:2212.10511 'When Not to Trust Language Models' (verified), plus arXiv:2402.13492: retrieval helps exactly when the answer is not guessable from priors, and hurts when it is. The proposal's thesis is that result carried into an embodied agent with the guessability variable manipulated rather than observed, which is a real methodological step up but not a new idea in kind, and it is missing from the proposal's home-vocabulary search. Verified as not-a-collision: RAP arXiv:2402.03610 (2024-02-06, cit 98) has no fixed-exemplar or compiled arm; arXiv:2606.04391 (state-grounded dynamic retrieval, web agents) keys retrieval on page state but never manipulates whether state matters; arXiv:2607.14514 VTM-Nav reuses cross-episode object locations in fixed scenes with no static control; arXiv:2602.08316 SWE-ContextBench and arXiv:2605.22219 SGR-Bench observe relatedness/state-gating rather than manipulating it; arXiv:2607.10608 (compliance trap) and arXiv:2603.21520 MemAPO, arXiv:2605.24117 SkillEvolBench also verified and off-target.
reviews.strongest_objection: P2, the prediction that carries the whole 'demand gates the residual' thesis, is close to already falsified by the node's own Measurement C, and the proposal never reconciles the two. Measurement C (in the brief, binding) gives k3 - static3 = +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4] and instr_all only +2.9 below static3, so retrieval currently beats the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt by roughly +20 net in the canonical, loose condition. P2 asserts that in canonical x 25 the scene-query minus type-agnostic residual is <= +8. That requires tightening the budget from 50 to 25 steps to erase about 12 net of measured retrieval advantage, which runs the wrong way: a tighter budget normally raises, not lowers, the value of a retrieved trajectory. The brief states explicitly that 'a claim that the residual vanishes must name the manipulation that removes it'; relocation is a manipulation that is supposed to create a residual, and no manipulation is named that removes the measured +17.2 in the canonical cell. If P2 fails, the proposal's own text says the residual is not gated by demand and the headline dies - so the central claim is at serious risk of being decided by data already on disk. Compounding this: the headline P3 is close to definitional (the retrieved sibling literally contains the relocated receptacle and no static arm can), and the brief forbids predictions entailed by a definition; P6 is auto-confirmed whenever P3 nulls (both arms collapse to the static level, a shared-term problem the entailment check already flags); and P4's null is threatened for a boring reason, since relocated experts from other scenes demonstrate off-canonical search that the static prompt was never told about. Secondary but real: the relocation rule is deterministic per (scene, class), which manufactures a world in which a fixed key-value table is exactly the optimal artifact, so 'the table compiles the residual away' is built into the construction rather than discovered, and the proposal concedes the interesting regime (the row count at which a table stops compiling) is left to a separate ladder.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Re-anchor every residual prediction on static3, the measured best static arm, and state P2 against the measured +17.2 rather than an assumed null: either predict the specific magnitude by which canonical x 25 shrinks the measured residual with a mechanism for the shrinkage, or drop P2's demand-gating framing and reposition the paper as 'supply and query type decide', which the relocated-cell contrasts (P4, P5) can actually carry. 2) Add the type-conditioned static3 arm to canonical x 25 and relocated x 50 - the two cells P2 is read from - so retrieval-minus-best-static is computable there at all. 3) Add a distribution-aware compiled procedure arm (~30 tokens: 'the object may not be in its usual place; open and check off-canonical receptacles of these types first'), compiled from the same relocated pool. This is the cheap static competitor that makes P3 non-definitional: if a one-line rule captures the residual, the binding story is about search policy, not bindings. 4) Fix the thresholds the entailment check names: state P1 at +14 net, P5 at +14, and the exploratory whole-bank and stale-sibling predictions as <= retrieval - 14 / <= static - 14, since as written a zero effect cannot be distinguished from the predicted 8. 5) Guard the escalation against floor effects - at 15 steps k=0 may collapse in both conditions and compress every residual; pre-register a minimum k=0 success in the harder cell. 6) Say explicitly that P1's canonical-vs-relocated comparison is paired on the surviving games after planner-failure drops. 7) Run at least a two-point table ladder (20-row scene-restricted vs 274-row full, which is already an ablation, plus a padded 1,000-row variant) so 'compilability' is a claim about scaling rather than about one small table.
reviews.missing_baseline: A static arm that is told about the relocation regime, compiled by rule from the same relocated expert pool but carrying no per-instance binding - e.g. a one-paragraph procedure 'objects are often not on their canonical receptacle; open drawers/cabinets/fridge in this order before giving up'. Without it, every positive residual at relocated x 25 is confounded by the static prompt being ignorant of the distribution shift while the retrieved trajectory demonstrates it, and P4's scene-disjoint null is threatened by exactly this non-binding search heuristic. Secondarily, static3 (the node's measured best static arm) is absent from the canonical x 25 and relocated x 50 cells, so the brief's own rule - retrieval minus the best static alternative - cannot be evaluated in the two cells that produce P2.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's Preprint Collision Check is one of the better ones I have seen in this program: six queries, channels labelled, real ids, and a genuine home-vocabulary query without agent/memory words. I verified with the s2cli paper command every id its novelty argument leans on - 2402.03610 (RAP, 2024-02-06, cit 98), 2606.04391, 2607.14514, 2602.08316, 2605.22219, 2607.10608, plus 2603.21520 and 2605.24117 from the brief - and all resolve as described; 2505.16348, 2410.18195, 2603.09716, 2410.07071, 2606.22844, 2506.15635 and 2506.04579 surfaced incidentally in my own searches and match. I could not separately verify 2510.09883, 2411.18126, 2603.26775, 2603.24690 or 2506.06699; they are not load-bearing. My own searches, all answered by the s2cli channel (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace; WebSearch is unavailable in this session, so channel (b) was not used and no section text was read): (1) mechanism, --recent, 'manipulate instance-specific bindings object location experience retrieval agent versus static prompt' -> 2606.30457, 2603.09716, 2601.08605 (ExpSeek), 2505.16348, 2410.18195, 2512.22342; nothing that edits an environment to plant bindings. (2) closest named method, 'RAP retrieval-augmented planning contextual memory past experiences ALFWorld' -> 2402.03610 verified, plus 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2607.24097 MemChain, 2606.22844, 2605.30690, 2410.07071; none contrasts against a fixed exemplar set or a compiled table. (3) --recent, 'when is retrieval necessary procedural knowledge versus instance-specific knowledge agent memory ablation' -> 2608.14036 (the closest conceptual threat, see closest_prior_work), 2606.23127, 2605.18421 EvoMemBench (cit 7; reports long-context baselines still beating specialized memory, relevant to the whole-bank arm), 2604.27003, 2604.01348. (4) --recent, 'agent skills procedural anchoring versus missing knowledge injection' -> 2608.14036 again, 2607.22520 (The Regression Tax), 2603.15401 SWE-Skills-Bench, 2602.12670 SkillsBench - a visible 2026 cluster arguing that compiled skills give procedural stabilization rather than knowledge, which the proposal neither cites nor positions against. (5) 'counterfactual perturbation of embodied benchmark object placement to test memorization' -> nothing on PDDL-level relocation; closest were 2505.17127 (Visual CounterFact) and 2509.12718. (6) --recent, 'does experience retrieval beat a fixed prompt built from the same experience, matched tokens' -> 2605.12493 LongMemEval-V2 with AgentRunbook-C vs AgentRunbook-R at accuracy and latency, the strongest uncited threat to the compiled-table half of the claim. (7) home, 'retrieval helps only low-popularity facts' -> 2212.10511 and 2402.13492, the parametric-vs-nonparametric ancestor of the entire demand argument, absent from the proposal's home search. (8) --recent, 'compiled knowledge table in prompt versus per-query retrieval at matched token cost with caching' -> effectively empty for the table claim (2608.07458, 2604.02985 are efficiency work), which corroborates the proposal's own report of an empty result there. So: the specific PDDL-relocation manipulation appears unclaimed, but the collision check under-searched its own framing claim (the 2026 skills cluster) and its own home literature (Mallen-style guessability), and it misses a benchmark that already ships the compiled-vs-retrieved comparison at a cost axis. Novelty is scored on what I verified: the manipulation is new, the thesis is not.
